### Observed differences

- The activity set is stable: A20, A21, A22, A25, A30, A31 and A36 co-occur in 100 in 100 traces in both windows, so the differences below concern order and routing, not activities appearing or disappearing. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- A20's successors changed completely: earlier its outgoing transitions went to A30 (about 40 in 100), A31 (about 33) and A36 (about 28); in the later window about 99 in 100 go to A22, with A30 and A36 nearly gone (about 0.5 in 100 each). [DIR001]
- A21's successors changed completely: earlier A21 was followed by A25 in all cases; in the later window it is followed by A30 (about 36 in 100), A31 (about 33) and A36 (about 31), while A25 drops to about 1 in 100. [DIR002]
- The group A30/A31/A36 now hands over to A25 instead of A22: earlier each of the three still led to A22 in roughly 29–38 in 100 of its transitions; in the later window A22 is nearly absent as their successor (about 0.5 in 100) and A25 appears at about 31–36 in 100, while transitions among the three themselves continue at similar shares. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- The relative order of the group and A21/A22 reversed: earlier A30, A31 and A36 each ran before A21 and before A22 in 100 in 100 traces; in the later window A21 and A22 each run before all three in about 99 in 100. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- Event positions moved accordingly: A30, A31 and A36 shifted later (mean relative position about 0.41 to about 0.59), while A21 (about 0.62 to 0.53) and A22 (about 0.47 to 0.38) shifted earlier. [POS003, POS004, POS005, POS001, POS002]
- Two step distances changed exactly as this reordering predicts: A20 to A22 went from always 4 steps apart to immediately consecutive in about 99 in 100 cases, and A21 to A25 went from immediately consecutive to 4 steps apart in about 99 in 100 cases. [LAG001, LAG004]
- Four further distance items also qualified, but their later-window profiles rest on only 2 traces each, so they are not used as support. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG005, LAG006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Main hypothesis: the placement of the group A30/A31/A36 relative to A21, A22 and A25 changed. In the earlier window the segment ran A20, then the group A30/A31/A36 (in no fixed internal order), then A22, then A21, then A25 immediately; in the later window it runs A20, A22, A21, then the group A30/A31/A36, then A25. That is, A30/A31/A36 now execute after A21 rather than before it, A22 immediately follows A20, and A25 now follows the group instead of immediately following A21. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, LAG001, LAG004, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

Supporting signs: the order reversal is observed directly for all six activity pairs; the successor changes at A20, A21 and the three group members match it; the two distance changes are exactly what this reordering predicts; all five position shifts point the same way; and 22 items qualified against roughly 0.42 expected by chance in a stable process, so the pattern as a whole is not what random re-splits of unchanged traces produce. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, LAG004, POS003]

Limitations: the evidence shows the changed relative order but cannot establish which side "moved" — the group moving after A21 and A21/A22 moving before the group are descriptively equivalent, and the evidence cannot distinguish a single restructuring from coincident rerouting at A20 and A21. The A22-before-A21 order in each window is inferred from positions rather than a directly observed pair relation, the internal order of A30/A31/A36 remains unfixed in both windows, and four distance items rest on only 2 later-window traces. [POS001, POS002, LAG002, LAG003, LAG005, LAG006, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
